blocking.fix: Replace the universal rule with a per-instruction step table giving, for every lifted/control instruction: locations and memory cells read, locations/cells written, classical successor function of registers/flag (including conditional fault to HALT, lift.call target, lift.ret popped index, lift.retval HALT), frame fields occupied, and the inverse operation used in a reversed step (exchange back for assignments/stores, re-call for oracle_call, adjoint for perm_call, decrement/reverse bookkeeping for alloc/call/ret). Size the frame as the maximum total displaced width over all instructions, including memory-cell and oracle tgt/fr widths, and declare sp with width and bounds.
blocking.problem: The claimed construction does not cover its own instruction set. Several lifted instructions write more than the one location §3.6/§3.7 allows and do not have assignment semantics: lift.alloc writes w and heap_used, lift.call writes a stack cell, sp and depth, lift.ret writes sp and depth, lift.oracle_call XORs two locations, lift.perm_call transforms many mut locations in place. A frame with one displaced slot of width W_max (widest register) cannot retain all displaced values, cannot hold a memory cell or oracle target wider than W_max, and exch-back cannot invert an oracle_call or perm_call. §3.6 step 3 also gives no successor function for conditionally faulting lift.div/alloc/call/faultif, for lift.call, lift.ret or lift.retval, and sp is used in §4.2 but never declared in the step state. The sentence 'exactly one location changes per step' is false, so two executors must invent different realisations and frame layouts.

blocking.fix: Define lifted addresses completely: heap_base value, units of heap_used and n (bytes), counter widths (heap_used must represent heap_limit without wrap), the map from a ptr value to (region, cell index, byte offset) for every region in layout, behaviour for unaligned and multi-cell accesses, and the allocation-bounds test as a function of state the machine actually has (e.g. per-branch allocation metadata recorded in quantum memory, or restrict the defined test to region bounds and say the object-bounds model of the north star is producer-enforced differently). State lift.free's validation predicate and fault. For CC/R state the initial bump pointer and that free of a non-top allocation is a trap/fault or a defined no-op; pick one.
blocking.problem: No rule translates a lifted address into a quantum-memory access, and classical allocation is nondeterministic. lift.load/lift.store take address a in a reg[ptr], but qload takes a cell index wire[A]; heap_base is used in lift.alloc and never defined, H serves both as heap-region size exponent (§7.2, 2^H bytes) and heap_used counter width (§3.7, so heap_used=2^H wraps to 0), byte-versus-cell units and unaligned/multi-cell accesses are unstated, and the required range check 'against the declared allocation' has no per-branch allocation metadata to check against for bump allocation. lift.free 'validates only' without a predicate or fault. In CC/R the bump allocator's base address is unspecified, so ptrtoint observes different values in different executors, and free of a non-most-recent allocation has no semantics.

blocking.fix: State scope and lifetime: a qregion is either (a) function-local, created by image gates at entry, required to be back at its image before the creation gates are reversed to clean at exit, with name resolution local to the function and an adjoint rule (image gates reversed), or (b) an interface/object-level region passed in the signature with a linear memory token consumed and reproduced by qload/qstore/qexchm. Take (a) for heap/stack and add (b) only if persistent quantum memory (the SQLite database) is in scope, distinguishing them syntactically. Define nested/controlled creation (image gates under the active predicate, cells start clean and are freed clean, not at image, on the predicate-0 branch).
blocking.problem: A qregion's scope, lifetime and ownership are undefined, and its exit condition contradicts itself. §4.6 says a region is created at region entry and 'MUST be returned to its image at exit', §5.2 requires memory 'clean / at image' and its construction reverses step 1 (including image creation) so cells end clean, not at image; qfree can only release clean wires. Regions are declared in the object types section but appear in no function signature, so it is unstated whether a name is function-local or object-global, who owns it across nested calls, whether two calls share one region, what controlled creation does on the 0-branch, or what the adjoint of region creation is (absent from the §5.3 table). Memory still has no linear token or equivalent ownership rule.

blocking.fix: State the discipline correctly: in an action, borrowed wires may be used only inside subcircuits whose realised unitary on borrowed-plus-every-wire-they-touch is a permutation matrix (equivalently, borrowed wires never interact, as control or target, with any wire that is in a non-basis state at that point), OR keep the identity MUST but label the gate restriction necessary-not-sufficient and require a channel/permutation certificate over the borrowed-extended domain for every borrowing region. Take the first form as the well-formedness rule and keep the certificate for library frames; change §12 borrowed from discipline_checked to the domain and method by which identity was verified.
blocking.problem: The stated sufficient discipline for borrowed wires is mathematically insufficient in actions. §5.6 requires identity on borrowed systems (correct), but then claims permutation-gates-only plus basis restoration yields it 'by T3'. T3 needs the realised unitary to be a permutation matrix; in a general action it is not. Counterexample: prepare a data wire in |-⟩, cx with the borrowed wire as control, unprepare: the borrowed wire receives a Z (phase kickback), its basis value is restored on every configuration, only permutation gates touched it, yet |+⟩ maps to |-⟩. §12 records only borrowed.discipline_checked, so a conformant certificate can assert restoration on exactly this insufficient basis.

blocking.fix: Complete the transfer table for every instruction that can appear in an action body (oracle_call: tgt/fr become perm with S = ins ∪ {tgt} if the callee is permutation, else not allowed as dependencies; action_call to a permutation action similarly; qinplace; qstore/qexchm to a cell kill all dependency sets naming that cell; qregion cells versioned by store count). Rewrite the qxor rule coherently. Restate T5 as: g returns to |0⟩ and factorises from the remaining state; diagonal/controlled uses may have applied the corresponding diagonal phase to the remainder, which is part of the program's semantics.
blocking.problem: Provenance is still not a checkable static discipline and T5 is false as stated. The qxor transfer rule is self-referential ('unless t was perm with S ⊇ {s} ∪ S_t'); there are no transfer rules for oracle_call, action_call, qinplace, or qstore/qexchm (which mutate cells named in other values' dependency sets, with no versioning rule for cells); and T5 claims a cleaned value 'leaves the remaining state unchanged', but allowed uses change it: a diagonal gate on g, or g as control into a phase-eigenstate target, applies a nontrivial diagonal phase as a function of S to the remainder after cleanup. Cleanliness/disentanglement is what validity gives, not unchanged remainder.

blocking.fix: Give the R machine a dynamic value-history rule that works under loops: each executed instruction records every operand value that the inverse needs and that is not provably still live with the same dynamic value at reversal time; conservatively, lossy and comparison instructions record both operands, add/sub/xor record whichever operand is not retained live. Add history rules for oracle_call/action_call (inverse is re-call/adjoint with recorded classical args) and state clock read returns c before its own record increments it (or after; pick one).
blocking.problem: The 'nothing recorded' rows confuse static SSA with dynamic execution. In a loop, a block parameter or SSA operand takes a new value every iteration; icmp's result does not determine its operands and add's result determines an operand only if the other operand's value from that iteration survives, which next iterations overwrite. §7.4 records nothing for add/sub/xor/icmp/zext/sext on the ground that 'SSA keeps operands live', so a finite trace through a loop cannot in general be reversed from the specified history and T4's hypothesis cannot be met by the specified frames. The table also has no rows for oracle_call/action_call from R (§3.1 allows R to call Q regions), and clock read does not state whether it returns the counter before or after its own tape record advances it.

blocking.fix: Complete §16 to a full grammar: define line and one production per section kind (symbols, imports, data images as hex, devices, layout, schedule, certificate and coverage or an explicit embedded-JSON rule with canonicalisation), the opcode set with typed operands, negative integers, and finite-float lexical form. Define each hash's exact input bytes: SCC hashing by replacing internal references with the member's local name sorted lexicographically and hashing the concatenation in that order (or another stated algorithm); object_hash over all sections except certificate; target_hash and schedule_hash over their canonical serialisations, which must be defined in §8 and §11. Give schedule entries stable referents (function hash plus instruction index in canonical order).
blocking.problem: The one normative interchange form and all hashes built on it remain undefined. §16's grammar has section := 'section' NAME line* with 'line' never defined, the function production is unreachable from section, and there are no productions for symbols, imports, data, devices, layout, schedule, certificate or coverage sections, no opcode enumeration, no negative literals. §9.2 says references are replaced by their content hashes and an SCC is hashed 'as one unit in canonical order' without saying what replaces intra-SCC references (their hashes are what is being computed) or what the order is. object_hash, target_hash, schedule_hash and reference_program_hash (§11, §12) have no defined inputs, and bindings.object_hash sits inside the certificate section of the very object it would hash. §11's serialised schedule has no encoding and no way to name the cleanup/gate an entry refers to.

blocking.fix: Give the target file a concrete syntax (state it is the §16-style canonical text, YAML subset, or JSON with stated canonicalisation). Define cost functions in a small closed expression language (e.g. constants, k, epsilon, log2(1/epsilon), arithmetic and piecewise tables) or require tabular values per k/epsilon decade. Define gate costs per class or delete the costlier-class fallback and state cross_class replaces/adds the gate cost. Allow decompositions to be parametric (a named scheme with parameters) for mcx(k). Replace §8.5 with a conversion table: named Qualtran/Azure quantities to named resources with factors; anything unlisted imports as a new resource, full stop.
blocking.problem: A vendor cannot write a target description another implementation parses identically. The format is pseudo-YAML with no named syntax or canonicalisation; gate costs may be 'fn(k)' or 'fn(ε)' with no expression language, so mcx and rotation costs cannot actually be written down; decompositions are fixed gate sequences, which cannot express a parametric mcx(k) decomposition; §8.2's cross-class fallback ('the costlier class's cost') refers to per-class gate costs that §8.3 never declares (classes carry only qubit_second rates), and whether cross_class replaces or adds to the gate cost is unstated. §8.5's import rule still says only that aligning units 'are converted', with no conversion table.

blocking.fix: Name the fields normatively even if bit layout is deferred: bennett_arg as a tagged union (integer width+value, f64, qreg id, token id) matched in order to the entry signature; bennett_result as (classical results, fault code, measurements array, tape length). Restrict bennett_reverse: it is an error (BENNETT_E_INVALID_STATE) if the run performed any measure, or if any qreg the run touched has been prepared, freed, or used by a later run; state that run records (history, classical args of Q regions) are retained until an explicit bennett_run_close (add it) and that reverse of a mixed run reverses region invocations in reverse invocation order. State suspend/resume/reverse behaviour on completed or unknown run_ids.
blocking.problem: The launch ABI's data path and reversal validity are undefined. bennett_arg and bennett_result fields are deferred in §17 to 'those named in §10, §12, §13', but §10 never names them, so how classical arguments, qreg ids and budget tokens are passed to a CC entry, and what wait returns beyond prose, is left to each implementer. bennett_reverse is specified for pure tier runs, but a run is a CC entry that may invoke R functions, several Q regions and measure (in device CC); reversal after a measurement is physically impossible, no validity condition excludes it, invocation order for multiple Q regions and retention lifetime of run records are unstated, and 'modified since' has no defined detection mechanism.

criteria.change: Declare sp, the stack region's size discipline, and qregion scope/lifetime (B1, B3) so the state diagram is closed.
criteria.evidence: §3.2/§3.7 now define tiers, register file, budgets and step state precisely. But sp is used without declaration, qregion scope/lifetime is undefined, and the one-write-per-step state transition is contradicted by §4.2's multi-write instructions (B1).

criteria.change: Pin lifted address translation and allocation bounds (B2); that is the last place an implementer must guess semantics.
criteria.evidence: Classical, lifted, gate, memory, allocation and call forms now exist with fault behaviour, including sdiv overflow and shift totalisation. Address-to-cell translation, heap_base, lift.free validation and successor functions for conditional lifted instructions are still missing (B1, B2).

criteria.change: Replace the universal write-once step rule with a per-instruction step/inverse/successor table (B1).
criteria.evidence: The round-1 core failures are genuinely fixed: HALT self-loop, internal injective fault register outside the reversed prefix, permutation-only oracles, wire heap/depth counters, gate matrices with phase-exact decomposition legality. But the §3.6 construction cannot realise multi-write lifted instructions, and the §5.6 borrowed discipline is insufficient in actions (B1, B4).

criteria.change: Define the syntax of the target file and a closed expression language (or tables) for fn(k)/fn(ε) costs (B8).
criteria.evidence: Resource kinds with aggregation rules, a timing model, occupancy integral, borrowed-charge replacement and peak space budgets are now stated. Cost functions have no expression language, the cross-class fallback refers to undeclared per-class gate costs, and §8.5 has no conversion table (B8).

criteria.change: Complete the §16 grammar and define every hash's input bytes, including the SCC algorithm and object_hash excluding the certificate (B7).
criteria.evidence: Object sections, content-hash identity, imports by name+signature, frame descriptors, C launch and scheduling ABIs, and a machine-readable certificate are all present in shape. The canonical text grammar cannot encode most sections, hash inputs are circular or undefined, and the serialised schedule and bennett_arg/bennett_result have no encoding (B7, B9).

criteria.change: Restate T5 as factorisation-to-|0⟩ and make the reference interpreter define nested calls and lifted memory accesses by the same rules executors use (B5, B2).
criteria.evidence: §14 now has a per-basis reference interpreter, quantum state semantics with Born measurement, and T1–T6 with hypotheses; T2's sketch and T3's realised-permutation hypothesis are correct. T5 is false as stated, T4 rests on history frames that cannot reverse loops, and §14.1 does not define lift.oracle_call/memory semantics recursively (B5, B6).

criteria.change: Reconcile the reference binding's extra steps (edge movs, producer range checks) with the north star's statement that the budget counts reference steps on the materialised region, or state explicitly that the versioned mapping defines those steps.
criteria.evidence: No contradiction of substance with the north star remains: register-file oracles, fault construction, MBU-under-control fallback, device-side CC and launch reversal per tier all follow it, and Silq/Unqomp, QCM synchronisation and linear wire SSA are used in their established forms. The reference binding counts edge movs and producer-emitted range checks as budget steps, which sits awkwardly with north-star §4.2's materialised-region step unit.

criteria.change: Finish the encoding layer (§16 grammar, target-file syntax, schedule serialisation) so the text, not the authors, answers interchange questions (B7, B8).
criteria.evidence: A VM or specialiser author could start on semantics tomorrow; the document is organised where a reader expects rules and the rewrite is honest about deferrals. Interchange-level work (parsing objects, targets, schedules) still stops at undefined grammars and struct fields.

path_to_accept: B1, B2, B4 and B6 are the semantic core: a per-instruction step/inverse/successor table with a correctly sized frame and declared sp; a complete lifted-address and allocation-bounds definition with deterministic classical allocation; a correct borrowed-wire rule for actions (permutation-only interaction or certified identity) reflected in §12; and R history frames that record dynamically destroyed operands under loops. B3, B5 follow with one paragraph each (qregion scope/lifetime; completed provenance transfers and a corrected T5). B7–B9 are the interchange layer: a complete §16 grammar, defined hash inputs with an SCC algorithm, a target-file syntax with a closed cost-function language, and named bennett_arg/bennett_result fields with reversal validity conditions. With those nine fixes and no new contradictions I would return accept.
suggestions: Require gate angles to be finite f64 (NaN/±∞ make the §4.4 matrices undefined) as a well-formedness rule in §4.4.

§4.5 qinplace: require the supplied token's budgets to be at least those under which @g/@ginv are certified fault-none; otherwise a budget fault leaves t non-clean. Also make the example call follow §4.7's operand order (tk before ins).

Add adjoints for ctl-wrapped calls (adj of ctl is ctl of adj) and for qregion creation to the §5.3 table; note the adjoint qborrow→qfree change makes the adjoint use clean scratch, and reconcile with §9.3's 'same descriptor' claim.

§4.6 qloop while: as defined, cond cannot depend on wires the body modifies, so it is a conditional repeat, not a data-dependent while; either rename/relabel it or allow cond_i computed from body-modified wires provided each cond_i is retained and uncomputed after the flags, under §6.

State oracle_call-graph acyclicity explicitly in §5.1/suite F (mutually recursive lift.oracle_call would make the §14.1 interpreter diverge, since nested calls draw on separate tokens and no global depth counter).
Define the empty-body oracle (n=0, B=0): the §5.2 construction commits success with payload 0 while F_B as defined never reaches lift.retval; align the two.
§8.2: give a tie-break for 'any' among classes with equal qubit_second rate, and state the load-time error when a program names a class the target lacks.
§11: reproducibility 'from the request plus scheduler version' needs the request to carry a seed or a determinism requirement on the scheduler.
summary: Draft 0.2 is a genuine rewrite and the round-1 centre is fixed; what remains is a second layer of holes the new machinery introduces. Resolution of round-1 blocking issues — codex: B1 resolved; B2 resolved for HALT/dispatch/exit, but successor functions and multi-write steps are unresolved as new B1; B3 resolved (classical step count, wire heap/depth, nested token), address translation remains as B2; B4 mostly resolved, memory translation remains (B2); B5 resolved; B6 resolved (token-budget caveat in suggestions); B7 allocation resolved, memory ownership unresolved (B3); B8 the identity MUST is now stated but the claimed sufficient discipline is false in actions (B4); B9 mostly resolved, provenance transfers and T5 remain (B5); B10 resolved; B11 mostly resolved, R history and clock ordering remain (B6); B12 mostly resolved, cost-function encoding remains (B8); B13 mostly resolved, SCC/hash/grammar remain (B7); B14 resolved; B15 mostly resolved, reverse validity and arg/result fields remain (B9); B16 mostly resolved, schedule serialisation remains (B7); B17 mostly resolved, hash bindings remain (B7). Muse: B1 resolved (register file, as recommended); B2 resolved except successors (B1); B3 resolved including numeric codes; B4 resolved via the one-to-one reference binding and wire counters; B5 resolved; B6 resolved; B7 resolved in the recommended XOR-evaluator form; B8 mostly resolved (block-diagonal semantics, adjoint table, region-level ctl), qregion/ctl adjoints in suggestions; B9 mostly resolved, provenance completeness remains (B5); B10 resolved in the recommended explicit form; B11 partially resolved (forms/endian/images yes, address translation no: B2, B3); B12 partially resolved (device models, entropy tape yes; history rules flawed under loops: B6); B13 mostly resolved, cost-function/cross-class/import remains (B8); B14 partially resolved (hash identity yes; grammar still a skeleton: B7); B15 mostly resolved (run_id/prepare/free/suspend yes; struct fields and schedule encoding no: B7, B9); B16 mostly resolved (quantum semantics, T3/T6 restated; T5 false: B5). Opus: B1 resolved except multi-write step realisation (B1); B2 resolved in intent, heap layout undefined (B2); B3 resolved; B4 resolved; B5 mostly resolved (flag chain adopted; while restricted to unmodified condition wires, noted in suggestions); B6 mostly resolved (basis-diagonal criteria, MBU fallback), transfer completeness remains (B5); B7 resolved except mixed-run reversal (B9); B8 resolved except hash algorithm detail (B7); B9 mostly resolved, cost functions remain (B8). New blocking issues B1–B9 are concentrated in the step realisation for multi-write instructions, lifted memory, borrowed-wire sufficiency, R history, and the still-skeletal interchange encodings. Mean of my scores is 3.13, up from round 1, with C3 at 3: a competent, implementable-in-outline draft that is not yet stranger-implementable.
